entry.title: [NEW] MAL-2026-17875: Malicious code in monkey-tags-ip (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in monkey-tags-ip (npm)

Affected:

  • monkey-tags-ip

npm user 'conx3993' published this package in a dependency confusion campaign. It squats a name that looks like an internal package and uses version 53.4.1 so misconfigured resolvers pick it over the real one. Version 0.0.0-stage is an empty placeholder. A 'preinstall' hook runs 'ip.js', which poses as an IP geolocation helper. On install it sends an HTTPS GET to attacker-controlled host realwbx.com (/ip?f=json) with a hard-coded 'Authorization' value ('Bearer xHlT6gllTfGbKgdivAKTzWKxrILWlNlv') unique to this package, then discards the response. The token tells the operator which internal package name the victim installed, and the request reveals the victim's public egress IP.

entry.content:
Malicious code in @newspage/lib-ng-async-routes-ui (npm)

Affected:

  • @newspage/lib-ng-async-routes-ui

npm user 'priyashareek' published this package in a dependency confusion campaign against the internal scopes @accenturecodefoundry and @newspage. The publisher used 99.99.x versions to outrank the internal packages. 0.0.0-stage and 99.99.1 are empty placeholders. In version 99.99.4, index.js sends an HTTPS GET to attacker-controlled host accenture-npm.azurewebsites.net (/async). The same publisher's @accenturecodefoundry/mfe-pot-shared-ui-scds-core calls back to that host. The 'preinstall' script in these versions is empty; the publisher put 'node index.js || true' in the 'main' field instead, likely by mistake. Node.js can't resolve that 'main' target and falls back to index.js, so the beacon fires when code requires or imports the package, not during install.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-88h9-xgvx-hvf2: @grpc/grpc-js: The exact path match matcher incorrectly only applies a prefix match for case-insensitive matches
entry.content:
@grpc/grpc-js: The exact path match matcher incorrectly only applies a prefix match for case-insensitive matches

Aliases: CVE-2026-101914

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • @grpc/grpc-js-xds — fixed in 1.13.1
  • @grpc/grpc-js-xds — fixed in 1.14.1

### Impact When using RBAC to apply authentication rules, the exact path (method name) matcher applies a prefix match instead of an exact match for case-insensitive matches. As a result, if a service has a method with a name that is a prefix of the name of a different method, and they have different access rules, and case-insensitive matching is used, this bug can cause improper authentication. ### Patches This vulnerability is fixed in 1.13.1 and 1.14.1. ### Workarounds This problem can be avoided by enabling case-sensitive path matching.

entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-17865: Malicious code in passwordcrackv2 (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in passwordcrackv2 (npm)

Affected:

  • passwordcrackv2

passwordcrackv2 poses as a dependency-free Discord MFA library but pulls node-net-pool from the attacker's GitHub repo lunexindonesia/node-net-pool, and on load lib/cache.js runs `try{module['require']('node-net-pool')}catch(_){}` to execute it. On Windows, that index.js downloads a script from a limbomail.com attachment URL, saves it as a hidden winsvc.js under %APPDATA%, %LOCALAPPDATA% or %TEMP%, runs it via a hidden WinSvcHost.vbs, persists through HKCU Run/RunOnce, UserInitMprLogonScript and a Startup shortcut, and re-checks for updates every two hours. Amazon Inspector reported the same loader stub in discord-mfa-solver (MAL-2026-16100). The npm account kingsize published passwordcrackv2 and passwordcracker with identical code on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10.
